title: Chapter 173: Wake Him Up
html:
At the sound, Chen Ge slammed the door shut without hesitation. Cold seeped through the lock into his palm and spread across his body. He froze outside, listening for the source.

“It came from beyond the door, but I can’t tell which direction.” He imagined a masked monster dragging a corpse along a corridor. The scraping drew nearer—then stopped.

Every muscle tightened. The door felt like a mirror between two reflected worlds. On the other side, the monster might be standing in precisely his position. Only the door separated them, and neither dared move first.

An eerie wind moved through the corridor. Four minutes later, a door opened on the second floor. The nurse had caught up. Chen Ge could not abandon his position; the creature beyond the door had probably sensed him, and any sudden movement might draw it through.

A silent contest had begun. The creature hesitated inside while Chen Ge lacked any plan for confronting it. For now, he needed only to secure the door temporarily and survive until dawn.

After searching the upper floors, the dead nurse reached the first. She must have been vindictive in life; the moment she spotted him, she lurched into a run.

A madwoman in a tattered uniform charged through the sealed building’s darkness. Veins stood out along Chen Ge’s arms as he watched her approach from the corner of his eye.

“I’ve already given you the notebook, so why are you still chasing me?”

Elsewhere, he would not have panicked, but the unseen monster behind him exerted crushing pressure.

He had heard it without seeing it, and nothing inspired fear like the unknown.

The nurse came relentlessly, claws flailing. Within moments, only ten meters remained. Her cleaver wounds had healed, and her distorted body looked solid again. The lost wrist camera still hung from her uniform.

“Don’t push it.”

At five meters, he chose between the two threats. The nurse was weaker. He would handle her first, then confront whatever waited beyond the door.

He slowly released the handle. Once she came within reach, he rushed her faster than she had charged him. The hammer swung in a furious barrage. Despite her resilience, the nurse was not especially powerful.

When the cleaver bit into her form, he did not press the attack recklessly; the greater danger remained behind him.

As they fought, Room 3’s door began to bleed. Crimson rivulets ran down its surface and vanished upon touching the floor. A powerful force pushed from within, and the hinges creaked as the door inched open.

“It’s coming out.” Several seconds had not been enough to finish the nurse. Now Chen Ge was trapped between two threats while she coiled her mangled body around him like a constrictor.

With a greater danger behind him, he hardened his resolve, tore free, and drove the hammer into her back. The black phone’s weapon weakened ghosts; repeated blows to the same spot hurled the nurse forward, directly between Chen Ge and the blood door.

The door was already half open, and something was coming out.

“You don’t belong here.” He continued driving her backward. Ordinary weapons could not kill her, so he tried the only remaining option: force her through the blood door and hope that doing so would help close it.

The plan succeeded more easily—and more horribly—than expected. As she neared the opening, a hairy hand lunged out toward the spot Chen Ge had occupied moments earlier. During the struggle, he had deliberately switched positions with the nurse.

The hand seized her and jerked her backward. Her face contorted, but she had no time to struggle before vanishing through the doorway. Chen Ge rushed forward, slammed it shut, and braced it with his full weight.

BANG!

Something pounded from the other side. He had endured the same assault at his Haunted House, but that door existed for only one minute. This one might remain until dawn.

BANG!

A violent impact numbed his back. “What kind of monster is in there? How can it be this strong?”

He did not know how to close the door, and nothing nearby could barricade it. Worse, the noise might attract other entities.

“I have to seal it, even temporarily, or I won’t survive until sunrise.” Forcing himself calm, he kept his back against the door and called Doctor Gao. “Please answer.”

It was answered after four rings. Doctor Gao’s voice drifted through the phone. “Chen Ge?”

The weak signal broke Doctor Gao’s voice into fragments, heightening Chen Ge’s anxiety. “Get Men Nan. This is an emergency.”

“He is still hospitalized, what do you want from him?”

“It’s life or death. He was born in a psychiatric hospital, and his hidden child personality is the original Men Nan.” The claim confused Doctor Gao, but urgency in Chen Ge’s voice conveyed the danger.

“I’ll drive there now. Give me twenty minutes. Stay on the line and tell me what you need.”

“I may not have twenty minutes.” Pain spread across Chen Ge’s back, and strange noises stirred in the neighboring rooms. “You have to awaken Men Nan’s youngest personality.”
